title: My browser voxel engine: a 16 km island of 25 cm voxels in three.js (trailer rendered in-engine)
author: trissytriss
selftext:
Ravensfell is a free voxel RPG on my own three.js engine: a 16 km island with towns, ruins, caves, magic, creatures and a dragon. I'm a software engineer, and I built it in about a week directing Claude Code. Voices are ElevenLabs. The trailer is rendered in-engine.

AI wrote the code. The taste was the job. Here's what I learned:

\- Show it a picture. A reference image beats paragraphs of adjectives. Most of the creatures started that way.

\- One small piece at a time. Ask for the whole thing and you get the average of the internet. Ask for something you can judge, then say no a lot.

\- Look at the result yourself. It told me a river connected to a lake. My screenshot showed a bank in the way: it had misread its own numbers.

\- Check every claim. It put "10,000 buildings" on my landing page. There are about 500.

\- The word you leave out is the bug. My first voices sounded like an old radio, because I hadn't asked for a close-mic studio recording.

\- It's fast at being wrong too. I asked it to refresh every character. It mangled their faces and wrecked their genders, and I had to undo the lot.

\- Turn every mistake into a rule. The list of rules ended up worth more than any prompt.

Free in your browser on a laptop or desktop, no download or sign-up: [https://ravensfell.online/?ref=r-aigamedev](https://ravensfell.online/?ref=r-aigamedev)

What's your workflow? And if you play it, tell me where it still feels like AI made it.
